summary: Long-tail latency in JSON output mode after escape-sequence tokens cause finalization backpressure
description: Issue summary: Customers report sporadic long-tail latency (final token delay of 2-8s) for responses emitted in structured JSON mode. Impact: Several request streams for a single enterprise customer (TextFlow AI) time out at the client after finalization delay, causing failed ingestion of generated JSON payloads. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east; affected across two model variants. Observed behavior: majority of tokens stream normally but final chunk stalls unpredictably, often when the decoded output contains backslash escape sequences (\n, unicode escapes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a structured output request with mode=json and schema validation enabled.
2) Use a prompt that requests multi-line JSON with escaped characters (e.g., user text that includes newlines and quotes).
3) Send requests at production QPS seen from customer (burst of concurrent requests ~60).
4) Observe streaming response: last event is delayed by multiple seconds before finalization event and content-length header closure.

comments: Asha Mehta (Customer): Customer noticed spikes after upgrading to SDK v1.9.1; intermittent and hard to reproduce locally.
Diego Ramos (Support): Thanks Asha — we've assigned this P1 to runtime. Can you provide an example prompt and the full request payload?
Asha Mehta (Customer): Provided example payload and raw response ids. Attached in linked Confluence page.
SRE Oncall (SRE): Initial traces show decoder loop re-entering escape-unmarshal path. Suspect backpressure in JSON postprocessor when encountering long escaped sequences.
Diego Ramos (Engineer): Reproduced in staging with high concurrency and escaped unicode sequences. Adding instrumentation to measure decoder buffer flush timing.
Diego Ramos (Engineer): Created PR to add a fast-path for escape sequences to reduce callback hysteresis: see related PR. Deploying to canary now.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: JSON-mode postprocessing holds a lock while performing validation/unescaping which blocks the streaming finalizer under burst load.
Telemetry: p99 finalization latency spikes correlate with requests that contain more than 40 escape tokens in final 200 characters.
Reproduction: Deterministic repro in staging by issuing 50 concurrent requests with payloads containing repeated \uXXXX unicode escapes; reproduces 80% of runs.
Checks performed: GPU/CPU and network metrics show no resource saturation; kernel traces show blocking in decoder postprocess call stack.
Workaround tested: Disabling schema validation in JSON mode removes the long-tail delay in staging; however not acceptable for customer's production schema needs.
resolution: Workaround applied: temporarily route TextFlow AI's traffic to a canary variant with escape-sequence fast-path enabled (serving-runtime PR #2048). Root cause: JSON-mode unescape+validate path held a mutex while performing regex-based unescape on long escape-heavy tokens, causing finalization backpressure under concurrency. Permanent fix: landed and merged PR to break unescape into lock-free streaming pipeline and added unit + integration tests covering heavy escape sequences. Rolling out to dedicated pool in us-east with monitoring for p99 finalization latency. Customer notified and will monitor for 48 hours before closing. Follow-ups: add a regression test to CI and update runbook with mitigations.
